findings.claim: The design's premise that the census supervision-snapshot verifier is already pair-aware is false. run.go:284 is only the inventory-record join, and run.go:629 only verifies announcements. The guest gate separately verifies owner/watcher/reaper through seconds-only identityAlive, so a btime step can still produce supervision-not-live after arming.
findings.fix: Extend supervision state identities with pidStartTicks/bootId, populate them for owner and components, parse them in readSupervisionSnapshot, and pass a complete Ref into a pair-aware identityAlive/AliveRef. Preserve seconds fallback for old state and Darwin.

findings.claim: arm-supervision persists its owner lock with seconds only, then uses that record for join, rearm, shutdown, and takeover decisions. Passing a pair only through the initial main identity does not protect these later arming-chain comparisons, and a clock step could misclassify a live owner and authorize takeover or signalling.
findings.fix: Carry the pair through wait_for_start_identity, write-owner-identity, owner.json reads, identity_alive, and stop_identity. Add optional pair fields to write-owner-identity and reject partial pairs; old owner files must retain seconds fallback.

findings.claim: The proposed Announce behavior is underspecified against the current four independent identity reads: StartedAt, ProcessCommand, and two ProcessIdentity calls. Recording a 'fresh authoritative probe' is unsafe unless start, pair, and command hash come from one probe; PID reuse between reads can bind identity fields from different processes.
findings.fix: Call ProcessIdentity exactly once before locking, validate the caller Ref against that result, and use that same result's StartedAt, StartTicks, BootID, and Command for MainId, Announcement, duplicate matching, and lease claiming.

findings.claim: The design says the recorded announcement uses the fresh second, but current construction derives both MainId and PidStartedAt from the caller's start. Without explicitly naming these assignments, an implementation can remove the equality gate yet still store the stale caller second, contradicting the stated safety property and leaving seconds-only downstream readers split from the announcement's pair.
findings.fix: Specify that both mainID's start component and Announcement.PidStartedAt use the single fresh ProcessIdentity.StartedAt value; define whether retire continues accepting the caller's old second or must use pair-aware matching.

findings.claim: The required old-reader/new-record compatibility is not achieved by the design. A new announcement records a freshly probed second, but an old binary authenticates announcements by seconds; after another btime step its new probe will differ and it will fail to recognize the same main. Additive pair fields only make new readers compatible with old records, not old readers compatible with drifting new records.
findings.fix: Either explicitly drop cross-checkout old-binary behavioral compatibility as impossible under second drift, or provide a rollout/version boundary ensuring all readers are pair-aware before new records are written. Add a mixed-version acceptance test if compatibility remains required.

findings.claim: Optional --start-ticks and --boot-id flags permit a partial pair unless validation is specified. Silently falling back to seconds when exactly one field is supplied turns truncation, quoting errors, or a missing Darwin field into weaker identity verification rather than a usage error.
findings.fix: Define pair presence as atomic: both nonzero/nonempty or both absent. Reject partial pairs in proc alive and lease announce. On Darwin omit both flags or pass the explicitly defined absent representation; do not pass an empty argument ambiguously.

findings.claim: The --start-time supplied path has no source for ticks and boot ID. Current mission/fixture callers commonly pass only --start-time, so merely changing the default derivation at line 359 leaves those calls on the flaky seconds path and fails the claimed complete arming fix.
findings.fix: When --pid is present, always take one paired live probe. If --start-time was supplied, validate it only under the legacy contract or replace it with the probe's fresh second while using the probe pair; document this behavior and update mission-driver and fixture call sites to pass an atomic pair where identity must remain caller-bound.

findings.claim: The proposed census.Alive fixture tests only the direct proc-alive seam and cannot catch the still-seconds-only supervision snapshot path. Fixture identities also carry no pair, so existing supervision fixtures cannot deterministically exercise pair comparison or btime drift.
findings.fix: Add a production-shaped snapshot test whose owner/watcher/reaper records and live processes carry unchanged pairs but differing seconds, plus mismatch tests for each component. Extend the fixture probe/schema to carry pairs or inject a Prober directly so the test is deterministic.

findings.claim: Choosing proc started-at --emit pair is materially better than proc probe as currently implemented: proc probe JSON does not emit StartTicks or BootID at all, despite the design presenting it as an equivalent option.
findings.fix: Require started-at --emit pair, or first extend proc probe to output startTicks and bootId and specify robust JSON extraction. Test Linux output and the Darwin empty-pair representation.

summary: The design removes the two named comparisons for the initial announcement path, but it does not complete the arming/verification chain. Most importantly, supervision owner and component identities remain seconds-only in owner.json and state.json, and the census snapshot verifier still calls seconds-only identityAlive; the cited pair-aware locations cover inventory joins and announcement pruning instead. Announce also needs a single authoritative probe and explicit fresh-second assignments, partial-pair validation, a defined supplied-start policy, and an honest mixed-version contract. The acceptance plan must directly exercise drifted supervision snapshots rather than relying on pairless fixtures or repeated timing-sensitive runs.
